WHOLE-GAME critique r1 (tag whole-r1) — COMPOSITE SCORE 34/100. Blind A/B 18/18 (100% detection, zero hesitation on any pair). Verdict: real modules, real world, real HUD, but half the 17-shot battery is unusable and the pieces do not agree with each other. BIGGEST GAP: postfx's 58%-authority content meter injects a multi-stop content-dependent gain over a look whose identity is FIXED exposure + fog — kill it (uMeterAmount 0.58->0, drop the 1x1 meter ping-pong and the 2.6/1.1s adaptation) for a pure depth-keyed open loop. Proven by A/B: ?meter=0 already takes deep-void median 24.5 -> 5.4 vs the reference's 6.1. Targets: dropoff median 71.5->11 (ref 10.7), godrays 196.5->54 (ref 53.7), p99.9 in every deep frame 248-255 -> <=110 (ref 99-107), descend-route cell-to-cell median variation 49x -> <3x. CROSS-CUTTING: over 15s of ordinary swimming from 38.7m to 28.2m the frame median goes 43.8 -> 3.1 -> 31.6 -> 25.7 -> 26.6 -> 153.4 (postfx meter x underwater canopy occlusion; uEvMax=1.0 below 30m means a dark frame can never recover). Vertical axis STILL flat: top:bot 1.38-1.99 across every underwater shot vs reference 8.62 (godrays-1) / 3.5 (kelp-forest-1). First-person viewmodel is not in the medium — the flashlight is the brightest object in frame at 680m. PLAY: unassisted dive reaches ~64m horizontal from spawn (2.9 m/s x 22s on 75 O2 at 1.67/s); the seabed is -300m at r=300 and -1369m at r=800, so the entire deep world is unreachable on foot. postfx THREW on route=explore ('Unexpected identifier gate') — whole post chain dead for that run. PERF: 7/18 shots under the 60fps budget (surface-pod 20, surface-above 20, shallows-floor 20.8, shallows-reef 26.1, seamoth-cockpit 43.9, grand-reef 46.9, seamoth 47); draws 208-695 (under budget); tris 1.56M-9.27M. Cost is postfx: ?nopostfx=1 takes surface-above 25.2 -> 89.1 fps (28.5ms/frame), shallows-reef 46 -> 57.7, shallows-floor 63.7 -> 69.6. Top 3 to fix by leverage: postfx, underwater, flora+structures.

Bypass repair is real and verified: ?nopostfx=1 godrays water rails clipAny 78.1-80.1% (clipRGB up to G 80.1 / B 71.7, p90 250), ?nopostfx=1&exposure=0.22 reads clipAny 0.00-0.13%, and the knob is an exact scalar (0.22 vs 0.44 = 2.0001-2.0003x linear luminance, linear G/B identical to 4 digits). whitenW ships as claimed: 9 shots identical to ?whiteneutral=0 on every column except p99.9 — hud 238.1->233.5 and shallows-reef 240.8->240.2 (both TOWARD shallows-reef-1's 235.3), seamoth 234.1->233.4. No regression anywhere: cave/deep-void/grand-reef/kelp/wreck bit-equal to r30.
postfx.gap: The stated gap is derived against the wrong plate. 'Our godrays water red 0.94-1.18% vs godrays-1's 0.06-0.19%' compares a 40 m open-ocean shot to a 150 m frame at the one depth in LOOK.md's whole ramp where red is authored to exactly 0 (#00AA9C). At our own measured G/B of 0.780, LOOK.md authors #2C9BC8 = RGB(44,155,200), R% 22.0; we deliver R% 8.7. The sign of the standing red gap is backwards. Also: four consecutive rounds (28-31) have now been spent on colour-metric epistemology with no pixel improved — fix tools/measure.mjs to decode per pixel to linear before averaging, publish clipAny with every statistic, and give the next round a target derived from a window that matches OUR shot's depth and biome.

biomes.verdict: grand-reef LANDED and I reproduce it twice: on the builder's own water-only window ours px(120,360)-(460,660) vs grand-reef-2 px(600,64)-(1085,250), ungraded went 47.81 -> 36.55 against a plate at 35.6-38.7 (1.31x -> 1.01x), and the whole clean column now runs 43.4->33.2 against the plate water's 39.8->33.8. cave and shallows-reef ungraded are bit-identical to r27 on every column, so the no-regression claim is true. KELP IS A QUARTER-FIX ON A KNOB THAT CANNOT FINISH. Same window px(640,0)-(800,340): G 248.9 -> 208.2, lum 212.4 -> 163.2, against clean water in kelp-forest-1 px(20,60)-(110,170) at lum 44.2/G 58 and godrays-2 px(1080,180)-(1200,360) at 48.1/G 61 - still 3.7x, at 55m against plates at 15-29m. Two-point fit through the sRGB curve says only 55% of that window's linear green is level-driven: at level=0 it still reads G~174 vs a target of 46-83. The header admits a floor (G~127) and simultaneously claims 0.40 puts the blended far field at G 72 and the window was never re-measured after the change - the number the defect was defined on was not checked. G/B 0.660 at grand-reef was called a hit off a LOOK.md hex; the plate window says 0.522 on five separate windows, so it is a 1.26x miss and the brief's own rule was not applied to it.
biomes.gap: kelp water level, 3.7x ungraded / 4.3x graded on water-only windows. level scales fog+scatter only; kelp_forest's light budget - skylight 0.82, the same class of term that fixed grand_reef's ambientFloor - was never tested, and neither was the safe_shallows leak's contribution to LEVEL (only to blue). Measure px(640,0)-(800,340) after every change.

terrain.verdict: The caustic net is the one claim that fully reproduces — a runtime ablation of uCausticsStrength on a frozen frame gives 2.02:1 peak-to-shadow on terrain-only near sand, exactly LOOK.md's target — but the round's actual objective failed: at matched metre scale (raycast: 0.40 m per 100 px, camera 3.9 m off the sand) our sand is still a soft 0.1-0.25 m camouflage mottle with no grain against the reference's uniform 1-3 px granular speckle, and the headline -13.7%/-14.5% A/B does not reproduce because changing terrain.js reshuffles the shared RNG and moves every plant in the crop.
terrain.gap: The asset still has no surface: on terrain-only pixels (every other mesh hidden at runtime, same frozen frame) tileContrast/mean is 35.6-37.3% against the reference sand's 6.0% bright / 26.7% at matched mean luminance, and r7 lowered fine, mid, net AND coarse bands together by 5-20% instead of trading hard-edged contrast for broadband grain — detailRMS/mean fell 12.3%->10.7%, the wrong direction. The wired-in surface microstructure measures 1.12:1 on sand and 1.01:1 on the drop-off rock, i.e. inaudible exactly where LOOK.md wants material identity.

flora.verdict: Round 33's buildGrass rewrite is real and verified — ribbed blades with a midrib, twist and collar, sized into LOOK.md's band, turf up from a 15000 cap to 20963/26199/24597 clumps — but flora's own surface grain carries ~2x the reference's octave energy and buries that geometry under hard-edged pepper, and the creepvine is still black origami.
flora.gap: Flora's own microstructure amplitude: near-plant window --crop=0.05,0.15,0.20,0.60 measures detail 24.53 / tileContrast 21.13 / octaves [12.48,13.94,17.38,21.16,22.18] against kelp-forest-3 --crop=0.10,0.60,0.30,0.95 at 22.70 / 11.83 / [6.45,6.36,7.00,8.59,12.09]; ablating with floraiso=1&flnosurf=1 takes detail 20.69->11.53 and the finest octave 11.30->7.18, and the grain-off tuft is visibly the better plant at 9x.

structures.verdict: Lifepod chroma and the cap profile are real, reproducible gains, but the wreck rebuild was refused on a hull window that is 25% non-hull and that is 1.5-3x the plate on every octave, and at magnification our plating has no plate tessellation at all.
structures.gap: Hull plating has no plate-to-plate tonal grid: texHull deliberately gives every plate identical albedo and SURF.hull.scale=0.006 caps surface.js at 0.30 m, so nothing in the pipeline can make the 2 m tessellation that is wreck-1's dominant read.

creatures.verdict: The reef eye and the grand-reef emitter now read; the flagship reaper does not - at 8x its eye is a gasket, its teeth are flat slabs, and at G/B 2.53 against water at 0.90 the animal sits outside its own medium.
creatures.gap: Creatures are chromatically detached from the water they swim in: head window 881,391,178,188 gbLin 2.532 vs its water 60,60,90,70 at 0.903 (2.80x), where reference creature-close-4 reads 0.770 vs 0.787 (0.98x). CN_FOG_SCALE=0.50 buys albedo authority by half-unfogging every creature.

schooling.verdict: The midwater is populated and the predator beat genuinely reads, but at 1x the schools resolve as low-contrast grey pepper rather than fish: fish-only crops measure luminance range 69-101 / tile contrast 4.3-5.6 against school-1.jpg's 154 / 17.0, and in kelp-forest the module is net-negative, darkening 17.2% of the frame with a speckle slab.
schooling.gap: Contrast DISTRIBUTION, not density: our fish blobs have a peak/median contrast ratio of 1.65 (median 16, p90 27) where the reference school measures 6.3 (median 15, p90 97). Make ~5-10 percent of fish flash to +80..+120 luminance over local water while the rest dissolve toward it, and cut the 27-61m population (2000 of 3360 fish, all 2-4.5 px) that only contributes noise.

movement.verdict: hullSlide is a real fix I reproduced bit-identically three times (Aurora hull, weld 7.267s -> 0.017s, travel 1.49m -> 27.33m) and the builder's refutation of the brief's _moveHorizontal attribution is correct, but blockNormal does nothing on an independent 48-face scan and the hull fix leaves the diver inside the wreck.
movement.gap: hullSlide restores motion without depenetration: at aurora-stern bearing 0 r15 never enters the collision shell (min standoff 0.619m = colRadius, 0/120 frames inside) while r16 is inside on 98/120 with the body centre 15mm from a triangle - a lid traded for a ghost.

survival.verdict: The loop finally has teeth and every number reproduces independently - crush kills at 7.5 HP/s on --route=deep (t=14.6s, respawn t=19.2s) and a quadratic 7.5->26 HP/s drown kills in 4.8s on --route=descend - but at 100m with a full tank the game is still completely silent, so the named '100m must be dangerous' defect closed only because the harness starts that route at 35% air.
survival.gap: At 100m on a full 135-unit tank: pressureStress 0.000, crushRate 0.00, warnings [] - 77.7s of air against a 30.9s ascent, a 2.5x margin, and no rim because SUITS.none=200m puts the amber band at 144m. Worse, NO shot and NO play route ever enters that 144-200m warning band (deep starts at 280m, descend tops out at 99.8m), so the continuous-pressure redesign's entire middle is unmeasurable by any tool in the repo. Lower SUITS.none toward ~140m or make the ascent tax bite on a full tank, and add a route or shot that sits at 160m.

tools.verdict: Scanner genuinely repaired and the node's cause correctly ablated, but the module's own headline feature still lights nothing and two self-claims fail on the frames the builder captured.
tools.gap: The flashlight casts no light: +0.31% on the cave floor and +1.33% on the night seabed at meter=0, against +134% on the tool's own head — the pass runs, at ~1/8 of a visible amplitude.

vehicles.verdict: Every published number reproduces on my own captures and the named defect genuinely moved (crushed 6.19% -> 2.34% over four boots, 2.317-2.399, against plates 0.015%/0.000%), and the postfx-AO root cause is proven by an ablation whose water control is byte-stable, but the shipped frame still shows two solid-black wedges across the inboard console faces, the interior midtones are still half the plate (p25 13.7 vs 29.7/26.8, median 34.6 vs 68.1/73.8), and the round never measured that DoF throws away 60% of the interior's own detail (MFD detailRMS 5.0-5.3 shipped vs 11.45 with DoF off vs the plate's 12.68).
vehicles.gap: The dashboard's two largest surfaces are still literally RGB(0,0,0); mean absolute deviation from the two plates across p10/p25/median/p75/p90/p99 is 27.4%, i.e. back to round 11's 27.2% rather than past it, and the exterior hull still carries 1.7x the plate's tileContrast (30.8/31.6 vs 18.2) and 2.2x its detail with every octave 2.4-2.6x hot, so the surface non-negotiable is untouched.

base.verdict: Real, independently reproduced gains - the base is finally an air source (O2 held 75 to 75 over 12 simulated seconds inside the observatory), clipping is gone, and 48 compiled fragment programs genuinely carry the surface term - but the headline exterior surface number was measured across a crop containing 15+ schooling fish and a ray fin, and on fish-free plating detailRMS fell 15.83 to 9.12 against the reference's 18.39.
base.gap: The night hull is the biggest miss and the one claim that is measurably false. On the base's own crop ours reads median 15.1 / p99 32.4 / detailRMS 3.09 / tileContrast 2.86 against night-shallows-1's base at 49.2 / 133.3 / 18.99 / 15.67: the real night habitat is 3.3x brighter in the body, 6x more detailed, and covered in lit window bands and cyan LED strakes, while ours is a near-black smudge. HULL_DEPTH_RESPONSE 0.34 plus exteriorShade cured the daylight ghost by deleting the night.

ui.verdict: Three of the four assigned defects are genuinely fixed and better evidenced than anything else in this repo — the setState latch provably refuses tools.js's openPDA, the marker cull drops labels 7 to 0 and reverts to within 1% when switched off, and the 280m/680m warning bleed no longer reproduces in the exact grand-reef to deep-void order — but the PDA glass only got halfway to hud-4.jpg and the blind trial was still 4/4.
ui.gap: The HUD's shape language, not its behaviour, is what gives it away: the vitals cluster trails two connector hairlines that end in near-invisible anchor dots on an element the reference never wires at all, the vehicle readout is three identical stacked parallelograms where seamoth-cockpit-1 has one two-cell asymmetric sheet (wrench+bolt sharing a row, temperature hooked below), and the depth bracket is a filled navy bowl measuring detailRMS 43.4 / sat 0.85 against the reference arc's 13.6 / 0.55.

audio.verdict: A measurably real, click-free biome soundscape (156 Hz in the abyss to 7011 Hz in air; waterline 448 to 7629 Hz in 1.2 s) wrapped around a game that never calls it: no module invokes ctx.get('audio'), so scanning, harvesting, crafting, pickups and the PDA are all silent while ui.js's private AudioContext plays square-wave beeps past the limiter, muffle and mute key.
audio.gap: The leviathan roar is inaudible exactly where it matters. Stereo-summed tap of the live master, 3 roars per site: Safe Shallows 12 m = +5.5/+6.7/+6.3 dB RMS (+8.4/+8.9/+8.1 dB peak) over a -24.6 dB bed, but Grand Reef 280 m = -0.9/-0.4/-3.7 dB over a -13.2 dB bed and Lost River 678 m = +0.1/+0.4/-1.3 dB over a -14.1 dB bed. Deep beds run 11 dB hotter than the shallows, the limiter already pins peaks at -5.0 to -5.4 dBFS in every biome, and spec.duck (0.34-0.38 over 2.2-2.6 s) is recovering before the call's 0.8-1.6 s attack peaks. Cut grand-reef-deep 1.0->0.45, lost-river-hollow 0.95->0.45, blood-kelp-dread 1.0->0.45, void-abyss 0.85->0.40, WATER.bellDeep +9.5->+4 dB, pressure drone 0.24->0.10 to land the deep bed near the shallows' -22 dB, and deepen the leviathan duck to ~0.12 held to t+dur*0.35, released over dur+1.5 s. Target >=+6 dB RMS and >=+8 dB peak at 280 m and 678 m. Same pass: gate the unprompted roar on hostility (safe_shallows is 0.05 and currently gets a reaper every ~158 s).

whole-game.verdict: 14/14 on the fair subset - removing the four unjudgeable pairs changed nothing. The leak was never the pairing.
whole-game.gap: Water SURFACE now decides more pairs than any other category (4 of 14): a hard black/cyan binary mask with no intermediate values, and sun glitter that is a perfectly regular orthogonal lattice of ~12 identical columns
